content.title: About
content.content: Bulgur is a whole‑grain product made from pre‑cooked, dried and cracked hard wheat. It retains most of the grain’s nutrients, contains no added fat, and has a light nutty flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bulgur is a staple in Middle Eastern dishes such as tabbouleh and kibbeh.
Because it is pre‑cooked, bulgur cooks quickly – just pour hot water over it and let it sit.
It comes in fine, medium and coarse grinds, each suited to different recipes.
Bulgur is high in dietary fiber, which supports digestive health.
Unlike rice, bulgur retains more B‑vitamins.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy bowel function, increases satiety and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates provide sustained energy, beneficial for athletes and active individuals.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron is essential for oxygen transport in the blood and for energy metabolism.

items.title: Provides magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes bulgur suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Bulgur contains gluten and is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Like many whole grains, bulgur contains phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption when consumed in excess.

items.title: Food allergies
items.content: Rarely, individuals allergic to wheat may react to bulgur.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bulgur can be added to salads, soups, side dishes, or used as a base for vegetarian patties. To prepare, pour boiling water over the grain (ratio 1:2), cover, and let stand for 10–15 minutes. It can also be toasted dry in a pan to enhance its nutty flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bulgur in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from moisture and light. Properly stored, it remains good for up to a year.
